newsitem.title: SPAIN: EMU secure though many will not meet criteria - Schmidt.
newsitem.headline: EMU secure though many will not meet criteria - Schmidt.

text.p: Former German Chancellor Helmut Schmidt said in an interview on Sunday there was only a small possibility that Europe's Monetary Union would not go ahead in 1999 even though many countries would not meet the criteria.
"There is an 85 to 90 percent chance that it will be achieved even though there will be countries that do not complete the five criteria, including Germany," he told the Spanish daily La Vanguardia.

Schmidt said the Maastricht Treaty, "a ridiculous document", was so loosely worded as to make the five criteria for single currency participation non-binding. "(The criteria) are not the most decisive issue as the Maastricht Treaty provides enough room for manoeuvre," he said.z
Schmidt, Social Democratic Chancellor from 1974 to 1982, said he was optimistic Spain and Italy would enter from the start in 1999.

On Britain's membership, Schmidt said he was confident it would join but not from the start. "I am convinced that (Britain) will be part of the single currency when it has been proven a success, but now it will be late."

European Union member states must meet criteria on inflation, exchange rates, long-term interest rates, budget deficits and total government debt to be considered for entry into EMU, according to the Maastricht Treaty.
